key_insight: A reinforcement learning controller can learn experiment-compatible measurement-and-feedback policies for quantum state preparation using only past measurement outcomes, without needing full quantum-state access.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, hardware-friendly preparation of target quantum states in real experiments, including many-body ground states and entangled resource states, with reduced reliance on handcrafted control design.
method: Use partial observability: policy conditions on the history of experimentally measured outcomes.
Choose both measurement operator and feedback action in real time via reinforcement learning.
Train with a stochastic terminal reward from one-shot measurements of randomly sampled Hamiltonian terms to estimate energy without full-state reconstruction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstration on ground-state preparation for the Bose--Hubbard model and on GHZ-state generation, indicating successful evaluation on representative quantum state-preparation tasks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of partial measurements and the practicality of sampling Hamiltonian components efficiently in larger or noisier hardware systems.
paper_title: Experiment-compatible measurement--feedback quantum state preparation with reinforcement learning
